drafts.name: Feynman expansion with exact graph symmetry factors
drafts.statement: For a finite-dimensional perturbative [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) with nondegenerate quadratic action and polynomial interactions, each coefficient of its [path integral](c:path-integral) with labelled linear insertions equals the sum of contracted graph amplitudes divided by their graph automorphism orders, with one propagator per edge and one interaction tensor per vertex.
hyps: The quadratic form is positive definite and each interaction tensor is symmetric.
The Gaussian contractions exist and are independent of the numbering of vertex slots.
The integral is read as a formal series in interaction couplings, with labelled external insertions.
Formal coefficients are finite sums, and labelled insertions determine the correct stabilizers.
steps: Expand the interactions coefficient by coefficient.

Expand each interaction exponential in its formal coupling. A coefficient with $n_i$ vertices of valency $i$ has denominator $n_i!(i!)^{n_i}$ from the exponential and symmetric vertex tensor conventions.
Pair all Gaussian slots to obtain decorated graphs.

Wick contraction pairs the external and interaction slots. Each pair contributes the inverse quadratic form, each vertex contributes its interaction tensor, and the power of $\hbar$ is fixed by the number of edges minus the number of internal vertices.
Count the labelled realizations of each graph.

The product of vertex permutations and slot permutations acts transitively on the labelled realizations of a graph. Its stabilizer is precisely the graph automorphism group that fixes external labels, including edge flips. Orbit-stabilizer cancels the expansion denominators and leaves the factor $1/|\operatorname{Aut}\Gamma|$.
app: Find the first quartic vacuum correction
Use a one-variable Gaussian of variance $\hbar$ with interaction $+g x^4/(4!\hbar)$ in the exponential.
Interpret the integral formally in $g$, with positive free quadratic coefficient 1.
The first coefficient is $g\langle x^4\rangle_0/(24\hbar)=g(3\hbar^2)/(24\hbar)$.
It equals $g\hbar/8$. The graph has one quartic vertex and two loops, with automorphism order 8.
The first quartic vacuum diagram has coefficient $g\hbar/8$.
drafts.citation: P. Etingof, Mathematical Ideas and Notions of Quantum Field Theory, MIT 18.238 lecture notes (2023).

drafts.name: Linked-cluster theorem for the logarithm of a perturbative partition function
drafts.statement: For a finite-dimensional formal [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) with Gaussian reference partition function $Z_0$, $\log(Z/Z_0)$ equals the sum over connected vacuum graphs of their amplitudes divided by graph automorphism orders. The [path integral](c:path-integral) expansion contains no disconnected graph in its logarithm.
hyps: The partition function is a formal interaction series with constant term $Z_0\neq0$.
The normalized series has constant term 1, so its formal logarithm exists.
Graph amplitudes multiply under disjoint union and use exact graph automorphism weights.
The automorphism of repeated components supplies the factorial required by exponentiation.
steps: Separate a graph into its connected components.
Every finite graph is a disjoint union of connected graphs. If a connected isomorphism type occurs $m$ times, permutations of those components contribute a factor $m!$ to its automorphism order.
Sum the multiplicities of each connected graph type.

For connected amplitude $a_C$ and automorphism order $s_C$, the contribution of all multiplicities is $\sum_{m\geq0}(a_C/s_C)^m/m!=\exp(a_C/s_C)$. Formal finiteness at each interaction coefficient permits multiplication over graph types.
Take the formal logarithm of the product.

The normalized full partition function is the product of these exponentials. Its logarithm is therefore $\sum_Ca_C/s_C$, with $C$ restricted to connected graphs. The Gaussian factor is removed before the logarithm and supplies no interaction graph.
app: Cancel a disconnected pair of vacuum diagrams
Suppose $Z/Z_0=1+a g+(b+a^2/2)g^2+O(g^3)$, with $b$ the connected second-order contribution.
The normalized partition function has constant term 1 and disjoint components have multiplicative amplitudes.
The formal identity $\log(1+t)=t-t^2/2+O(t^3)$ gives the order-$g^2$ coefficient $(b+a^2/2)-a^2/2$.
The disconnected term cancels and only $b$ remains.
The connected generating series is $a g+b g^2+O(g^3)$.
drafts.citation: P. Etingof, Mathematical Ideas and Notions of Quantum Field Theory, MIT 18.238 lecture notes (2023).

drafts.name: Normalization removes every vacuum component from perturbative correlators
drafts.statement: In a finite-dimensional formal [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory), a normalized [path integral](c:path-integral) correlator is the sum of graphs in which every connected component meets at least one labelled external insertion. Division by the vacuum partition function cancels all components with no external insertion.
hyps: The correlator and vacuum partition function use the same Gaussian measure and interaction couplings.
The external-free components contribute exactly the same vacuum series in numerator and denominator.
External insertions are labelled and the partition function has nonzero formal constant term.
The vacuum series is invertible and cannot permute with a component containing an external label.
steps: Split each graph into vacuum and insertion components.
The components with no external vertices form a vacuum graph. Every remaining component contains at least one fixed external label. This decomposition is unique for each graph.
Factor the weighted sum using the unique decomposition.

Graph amplitudes multiply across components. Automorphisms cannot exchange a vacuum component with an externally labelled component. The full numerator therefore factors as the vacuum partition series times the sum over graphs without vacuum components.
Divide by the invertible vacuum series.

The constant term of the partition function is nonzero, so formal division is valid. Its entire vacuum factor cancels, leaving exactly the graphs whose components all meet external insertions. The result does not require that the full remaining graph be connected.
app: Separate normalization from connectedness
For four labelled external insertions in a free Gaussian theory, compare the normalized four-point function with its connected part.
The Gaussian vacuum factor is nonzero and there are no interaction vertices.
Normalization retains the three pairings, each of which has two components that meet external labels.
The connected four-point function is instead zero, because no pairing joins all four insertions in one component.
Normalization removes vacuum components but does not remove disconnected components with external labels.

drafts.name: Tree and one-loop coefficients of the perturbative free energy
drafts.statement: For a finite-dimensional [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) action $S$ with a unique nondegenerate minimum $x_0$, normalized [path integral](c:path-integral) asymptotics give $\log(Z/Z_0)=-S(x_0)/\hbar+\tfrac12\log[\det B/\det S^{\prime\prime}(x_0)]+O(\hbar)$, where $B$ is the free Hessian and both integrals include $\hbar^{-d/2}$.
hyps: The real action has one nondegenerate interior global minimum, and contributions outside its neighborhood are exponentially suppressed.
The saddle expansion has one dominant term with positive Hessian.
The reference action is $x^TBx/2$ with positive definite $B$, and both partition functions use the same normalization.
The normalization removes the common Gaussian powers and fixes the determinant ratio.
steps: Expand the action near its unique minimum.

Write $x=x_0+\sqrt{\hbar}\,y$. The quadratic Taylor term is $y^TS^{\prime\prime}(x_0)y/2$, while the constant contributes $e^{-S(x_0)/\hbar}$. The odd cubic correction integrates to zero against the centered Gaussian.
Evaluate the leading Gaussian ratio.

The common factor $\hbar^{-d/2}$ cancels the Jacobian. Gaussian integration gives $Z/Z_0=e^{-S(x_0)/\hbar}\sqrt{\det B/\det S^{\prime\prime}(x_0)}[1+O(\hbar)]$. The outside contribution does not alter this asymptotic order.
Take the logarithm to identify the loop orders.

The logarithm separates the exponential saddle value and the determinant ratio. The term proportional to $\hbar^{-1}$ is the connected tree contribution, and the order-one determinant is the one-loop contribution. The remainder is $O(\hbar)$.
app: Compute a shifted quadratic saddle exactly
Let $S(x)=a(x-b)^2/2+c$ with $a>0$, and use reference action $x^2/2$.
The action has a unique minimum at $x=b$, with positive Hessian $a$.
The minimum value is $c$, and the determinant ratio is $1/a$.
The formula gives $\log(Z/Z_0)=-c/\hbar-(\log a)/2$, with zero remainder because the action is exactly quadratic.
The tree term is $-c/\hbar$ and the one-loop term is $-(\log a)/2$.

drafts.name: The effective action sums one-particle irreducible vertices
drafts.statement: In finite-dimensional formal [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory), the effective action is the quadratic action minus the exponential vertex series of amputated one-particle irreducible graph amplitudes. Its tree expansion reproduces the connected [path integral](c:path-integral) generating function, including every loop correction of the original theory.
hyps: The free quadratic form is invertible and the interactions are formal symmetric tensors.
The propagator contracts graph edges and the formal expansion is defined coefficientwise.
One-particle irreducibility means that the connected amputated graph has no bridge, and automorphism weights include external labels.
The bridge decomposition uniquely determines the effective vertices and their symmetry factors.
steps: Decompose a connected graph along all its bridges.

Remove every edge whose removal disconnects the graph. Each remaining component has no bridge, and the graph formed by these components and the removed edges is a tree. A cycle in this skeleton would contradict the definition of a bridge.
Replace each component by its amputated effective vertex.

Sum the amplitudes of all bridge-free components with the same number of external legs, including their automorphism factors and loop powers. These sums define the effective vertex tensors. The original propagator contracts the skeleton edges.
Recover each connected graph from the effective tree expansion.

Expand the tree series in the effective vertices. The unique bridge decomposition makes this substitution a bijection with original connected graphs. The vertex factorials and graph stabilizers preserve the original weights, so the tree-level effective action reproduces the full connected generating function.
app: Identify a reducible connected diagram
Consider two separate one-loop tadpole subgraphs joined by a single propagator.
Both subgraphs have interaction vertices, and the joining edge disconnects the graph when removed.
The joining propagator is a bridge, so the full connected graph is not one-particle irreducible.
The effective action stores the two bridge-free subgraphs as vertices. Its tree expansion joins them with the original propagator.
The full connected diagram is recovered from effective vertices but is not itself an effective vertex.

drafts.name: The effective action is the Legendre transform of the connected generating function
drafts.statement: For a finite-dimensional formal [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) with invertible free Hessian, let $W(J)=\hbar\log[Z(J)/Z_0]$ and $x=\partial_JW$. Its effective action is $\Gamma(x)=Jx-W(J)$ at the formal inverse $J(x)$. Thus $\partial_x\Gamma=J$, and $W$ is the inverse Legendre transform of $\Gamma$ for the [path integral](c:path-integral).
hyps: The source enters the action linearly as $-Jx$, and the connected generator has invertible Hessian at the expansion point.
The formal inverse function theorem defines the source as a function of the mean field.
The effective action uses amputated one-particle irreducible vertices and the same vacuum normalization.
The effective tree construction identifies its stationary value with the connected generator.
steps: Identify the linear source in the effective action.

A source is a one-valent vertex. No nontrivial one-particle irreducible amputated graph can contain such a vertex, because its incident edge is a bridge. Thus the effective action depends on the source only through $\Gamma(x)-Jx$.
Evaluate the connected generator at the effective stationary point.

The effective tree theorem gives $W(J)=Jx_0-\Gamma(x_0)$ where $\partial_x\Gamma(x_0)=J$. The invertible free Hessian makes this stationary point a well-defined formal series in $J$ and the interactions.
Differentiate the stationary value and invert the relation.

Differentiate with respect to $J$. The terms containing $\partial_Jx_0$ cancel by stationarity, so $\partial_JW=x_0$. Solving for $J(x)$ yields $\Gamma(x)=J(x)x-W(J(x))$. Its derivative is $J$, which proves both Legendre relations.
app: Recover the effective action of a free Gaussian
Take a free one-variable theory with Hessian $a>0$ and linear source $J$.
The Gaussian generator has invertible second derivative and the reference vacuum normalization is fixed.
Completing the square gives $W(J)=J^2/(2a)$, so $x=J/a$ and $J=ax$.
Then $\Gamma(x)=ax^2-a^2x^2/(2a)=ax^2/2$.
The Legendre transform recovers the free quadratic effective action.

drafts.name: 't Hooft genus expansion for Hermitian matrix integrals
drafts.statement: For a formal Hermitian matrix [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) with single-trace polynomial interactions and Gaussian variance $\hbar/N$, the connected free energy obeys $N^{-2}\log Z_N=\sum_{g\geq0}N^{-2g}F_g$. Each $F_g$ sums the oriented genus-$g$ ribbon graphs of the matrix [path integral](c:path-integral), with their automorphism weights.
hyps: The matrices are Hermitian and the interaction is a formal sum of single traces with the standard factor $N$ in the action.
Hermitian Gaussian contraction preserves ribbon orientation, and each vertex supplies one factor of N.
The free Gaussian partition function is divided out, and the expansion is coefficientwise in the couplings.
The logarithm selects connected graphs and finite coefficient sums permit a formal large-N expansion.
steps: Represent matrix contractions as oriented ribbons.
The covariance pairs $A_{ij}$ with $A_{kl}$ through $\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}$. Each closed index loop contributes $N$, each propagator contributes $1/N$, and each single-trace vertex contributes $N$.
Use the Euler characteristic of the ribbon surface.

A connected ribbon graph with $V$ vertices, $E$ edges and $F$ index faces carries $N^{V-E+F}$. Its orientable thickened surface has Euler characteristic $V-E+F=2-2g$, so the graph contributes $N^{2-2g}$.
Group the connected graphs by their genus.

The linked-cluster theorem removes disconnected graphs. At every fixed interaction coefficient there are finitely many pairings, so group their contributions by genus. Division by $N^2$ gives the even-power series. Its leading term sums exactly the planar ribbon graphs.
app: Read the powers of N from three ribbon surfaces
Compare connected diagrams that thicken to a sphere, a torus, and a genus-2 oriented surface.
Use Hermitian contractions and single-trace vertices with the N-normalization in the theorem.
Their Euler characteristics are 2, 0, and -2, so their unnormalized weights scale as $N^2,N^0,N^{-2}$.
After division by $N^2$, the three contributions scale as $1,N^{-2},N^{-4}$.
Only planar graphs survive the coefficientwise large-N limit.

drafts.name: Nonorientable surface expansion for real symmetric matrix integrals
drafts.statement: For a formal real symmetric matrix [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) with the Gaussian normalization of Theorem 4.7, the connected [path integral](c:path-integral) free energy sums twisted ribbon graphs with weight $N^{\chi(\Sigma)}$. Orientable and nonorientable surfaces both occur, so the normalized expansion can contain every nonnegative integer power of $1/N$.
hyps: The matrices are real symmetric with covariance proportional to $\delta_{ik}\delta_{jl}+\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}$.
The two contractions permit untwisted and twisted ribbon gluing.
Single-trace vertices and the Gaussian reference use the source large-N normalization, and interactions are formal.
The N-powers count faces, edges and vertices coefficientwise.
steps: Allow both ribbon identifications in a real contraction.
The real symmetric covariance has two index pairings. One preserves the local ribbon orientation and the other reverses it. The second pairing therefore introduces a twisted ribbon.
Count index faces without an orientability assumption.

Every closed index loop still contributes $N$, while edges and vertices contribute the same inverse and direct N-factors. Thus the total weight is $N^{V-E+F}=N^{\chi(\Sigma)}$ for the closed surface obtained by capping index faces.
Use the Euler characteristics of the possible surfaces.

For an orientable genus-$g$ surface, $\chi=2-2g$. For a surface with $k$ crosscaps, $\chi=2-k$. The connected logarithm therefore contains both even and odd suppressions after division by $N^2$, unlike the purely oriented Hermitian series.
app: Compare a projective-plane and a torus correction
Take one connected twisted-ribbon diagram on the projective plane and one on the torus.
The source real-matrix normalization applies, and both graphs are connected.
The projective plane has $\chi=1$, so its normalized contribution is $N^{1-2}=N^{-1}$.
The torus has $\chi=0$, so its normalized contribution is $N^{-2}$.
The real symmetric expansion includes an order-$1/N$ correction absent from the Hermitian genus expansion.

drafts.name: Harer-Zagier formula for Gaussian Hermitian trace moments
drafts.statement: For an $N\times N$ Hermitian Gaussian matrix $A$ with normalized density proportional to $e^{-\operatorname{Tr}A^2/2}$, the zero-dimensional [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) [path integral](c:path-integral) moment $P_m(N)=\mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}A^{2m}$ equals $\frac{(2m)!}{2^m m!}\sum_{p=0}^m\binom mp2^p\binom N{p+1}$ for $m\geq0$.
hyps: The matrix measure is the normalized Hermitian Gaussian with the stated covariance convention.
The measure fixes the polynomial moment and the orthogonal-polynomial weight.
The matrix size is a positive integer and $m$ is a nonnegative integer.
The finite moment expansion and binomial sums are defined for these values.
steps: Reduce the trace moment to a one-point eigenvalue integral.

The published proof uses the Gaussian eigenvalue density and its orthogonal-polynomial kernel. The trace expectation is the integral of $x^{2m}$ against the sum of the first N normalized Hermite polynomial squares times the Gaussian weight.
Compute the Hermite square generating integral.

Sections 4.5-4.6 evaluate the generating integral through the Hermite exponential generating function. The Gaussian completion of the square gives a finite binomial coefficient expression for each Hermite degree, rather than an asymptotic approximation.
Sum the Hermite degrees and extract the even moment.

The source sums the first N degrees and extracts the coefficient of the even generating parameter. The binomial sum simplifies to the stated formula. This outline cites the full orthogonal-polynomial calculation and does not replace it with an unproved Wick-counting assertion.
app: Compute the fourth trace moment at finite matrix size
Take $m=2$ and $N=2$ with the exact Hermitian Gaussian normalization.
The matrix size and moment order satisfy the theorem.
The prefactor is $4!/(2^2 2!)=3$. The inner sum is $\binom21+4\binom22+4\binom23=2+4+0=6$.
The exact moment is $P_2(2)=3\times6=18$, equal to $2N^3+N$ at $N=2$.
The finite-size fourth trace moment is 18.

drafts.name: Wigner semicircle law for expected Gaussian spectral measures
drafts.statement: For a normalized Hermitian Gaussian matrix $A_N$ with density $e^{-\operatorname{Tr}A_N^2/2}$, the spectral [path integral](c:path-integral) of this zero-dimensional [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) satisfies $N^{-1}\mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}f(A_N/\sqrt N)\to(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{-2}^2f(x)\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx$ for continuous $f$ of polynomial growth.
hyps: The matrices have the stated Gaussian Hermitian distribution and are rescaled by $N^{-1/2}$.
The scaling leaves finite limiting moments and suppresses nonplanar pairings.
The test function is continuous and has at most polynomial growth.
Polynomial approximation and uniform higher-moment bounds extend the moment computation to the stated test functions.
steps: Compute the limiting even and odd polynomial moments.

The ribbon expansion of a normalized even trace has weight $N^{-2g}$ at genus g. Only planar pairings survive, and their number is the Catalan number $C_m$. Odd moments vanish by the Gaussian sign symmetry.
Identify the measure and control its tails.

Direct beta integration gives $(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{-2}^2x^{2m}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx=C_m$. The exact Gaussian moment formula uniformly bounds every fixed rescaled even moment. These bounds imply tightness and uniform integrability of any fixed polynomial power.
Extend the moment limit to continuous polynomial-growth functions.

The moment limits determine the compactly supported semicircle measure uniquely. Approximate a continuous function by polynomials on a compact interval, then bound the outside contribution by a sufficiently high uniformly bounded moment. Increase the interval to remove that tail. This gives expected-measure convergence, not an asserted almost-sure law.
app: Find the limiting fourth empirical spectral moment
Set $f(x)=x^4$ in the Gaussian spectral law.
This test function is continuous with polynomial growth.
The exact rescaled trace moment is $N^{-3}P_2(N)=N^{-3}(2N^3+N)=2+N^{-2}$.
Its limit is 2, which is the Catalan moment $C_2$.
The expected normalized fourth spectral moment tends to 2.

drafts.name: Harer-Zagier orbifold Euler characteristic of once-pointed curve moduli
drafts.statement: For genus $g\geq1$, the orbifold Euler characteristic of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{g,1}$ is $-B_{2g}/(2g)$, where $B_n$ are Bernoulli numbers. The matrix [path integral](c:path-integral) proof in zero-dimensional [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) uses weighted ribbon-graph cells, not the Euler characteristic of the coarse topological space.
hyps: The moduli space parametrizes smooth genus-g curves with one marked point, with $g\geq1$.
The pointed mapping class group and its ribbon-cell model correspond to this precise moduli problem.
Euler characteristic uses orbifold stabilizer weights.
Cell automorphism orders must divide the alternating cell count.
steps: Construct the contractible complex of ribbon cell decompositions.
The published proof constructs the complex $Y_g$ and the action of the pointed mapping class group. Its cells encode ribbon decompositions, and the quotient cell count uses inverse stabilizer orders.
Express the alternating count through Gaussian polygon gluings.

The source relates the ribbon cells to the genus-refined counts of pairings on polygons. The Harer-Zagier Gaussian moment polynomial packages these counts, including their automorphism weights and the signs of cell dimensions.
Evaluate the weighted alternating sum using Bernoulli numbers.

Sections 5.6-5.7 compute the resulting generating series and identify its genus coefficient as $-B_{2g}/(2g)$. This outline omits the long cell-construction and generating-series calculation, both of which occur in the cited proof.
app: Compute the genus-two pointed orbifold characteristic
Take $g=2$ and the Bernoulli value $B_4=-1/30$.
The moduli problem is smooth curves with one marked point, with orbifold weights.
The formula gives $-B_4/(2g)=-(-1/30)/4$.
Its value is $1/120$. This rational number is consistent with stabilizer-weighted cells.
The orbifold Euler characteristic of $\mathcal M_{2,1}$ is $1/120$.

drafts.name: Brezin-Itzykson-Parisi-Zuber enumeration of quartic planar gluings
drafts.statement: Let $c_n$ count connected planar gluings of n labelled four-valent ribbon flowers with the slot conventions of the quartic matrix [path integral](c:path-integral). For $n\geq1$, $c_n=12^n(2n-1)!/(n+2)!$. This zero-dimensional [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) result counts planar maps with loops and multiple edges permitted.
hyps: The objects are connected planar ribbon gluings with labelled vertices and the source four-slot convention.
These conventions fix the factorial and avoid a count of unlabelled simple graphs.
There are n four-valent vertices with $n\geq1$, and loops and multiple edges are allowed.
The quartic potential produces exactly this class of diagrams.
steps: Represent the count in the quartic large-N free energy.
Use the matrix potential $U(x)=x^2/2+gx^4$. The coefficient of $(-g)^n/n!$ in the planar free energy is the number of connected gluings $c_n$ under the labelled flower conventions.
Solve the planar equilibrium density for the quartic potential.

The cited proof obtains the limiting eigenvalue density on a single interval and determines its endpoint from normalization. Integrating its fourth moment gives the derivative of the planar free energy as an explicit algebraic function of g.
Extract the coefficients of the algebraic free energy.

The source expands the endpoint relation and integrates the resulting series with zero interaction constant term. Coefficient extraction gives $c_n=12^n(2n-1)!/(n+2)!$. This is an outline of the matrix-density calculation, rather than a claim that planarity alone gives the factorial formula.
app: Check the first two quartic planar counts
Take $n=1$ and $n=2$ with the stated labelled four-slot convention.
The ribbon maps are connected and can include loops and multiple edges.
For $n=1$, the formula gives $12\times1!/3!=2$.
For $n=2$, it gives $144\times3!/4!=36$.
The first two connected planar gluing counts are 2 and 36.

drafts.name: Berezin change-of-variables theorem on superdomains
drafts.statement: For a smooth superdomain isomorphism $F:U\to U^{\prime}$ and compactly supported superfunction $g$, the fermionic [path integral](c:path-integral) obeys $\int_{U^{\prime}}g\,dv^{\prime}=\int_Ug(F(v))|\operatorname{Ber}DF(v)|\,dv$. In [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory), the Berezinian replaces the ordinary Jacobian for combined even and odd variables.
hyps: F is a smooth invertible parity-preserving map between real superdomains with fixed volume coordinates.
The super chain rule and the invertible even and odd bodies define the Berezinian.
The superfunction has compact support in the even variables.
Integration by parts in the nilpotent shifts has no boundary term.
steps: Factor the isomorphism into three elementary coordinate changes.

The published proof factors F into an ordinary change of even body coordinates, a nilpotent shift of even coordinates, and an odd-coordinate change with fixed even coordinates. The super chain rule and multiplicativity of the Berezinian reduce the theorem to these cases.
Check the even and nilpotent coordinate changes.

An ordinary even change uses the usual absolute Jacobian. For an even nilpotent shift, the Taylor expansion terminates because the shift lies in a nilpotent ideal. Each correction to the transformed integral is an even total derivative and integrates to zero by compact support.
Check the odd-coordinate case and compose the results.

Berezin integration extracts the coefficient of the top odd monomial. An invertible odd linear body changes that coefficient by its determinant, so the integration volume uses its inverse. The remaining nilpotent terms obey the same finite coefficient identity. Composition gives $|\operatorname{Ber}DF|$ for the full map.
app: Compare an even and an odd scale change
Use one even variable and one odd variable, with $x^{\prime}=2x$ and $\theta^{\prime}=3\theta$.
The map is invertible and the integrand has compact even support.
The super Jacobian is diagonal with even block 2 and odd block 3. Its Berezinian is $2/3$.

The transformed integral of $g(x^{\prime})\theta^{\prime}$ has integrand $g(2x)3\theta$ and volume factor $2/3$. The top coefficient is $2g(2x)$, whose even integral equals the original integral of $g$.
The inverse odd determinant is necessary for the substitution formula.

drafts.name: Fermionic Wick theorem as a Pfaffian contraction formula
drafts.statement: For an invertible antisymmetric form B on $2m$ Grassmann variables, the normalized Gaussian fermionic [path integral](c:path-integral) of $\lambda_1\cdots\lambda_{2r}$ is $\operatorname{Pf}(B^{-1}(\lambda_i,\lambda_j))$. Odd products have expectation zero. This [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) contraction law includes the pairing signs fixed by the order of the odd insertions.
hyps: The antisymmetric form is invertible, and the Grassmann volume order is fixed in numerator and denominator.
The normalized Gaussian exists algebraically and its contraction is the inverse form in this convention.
Each insertion is a linear odd function and their written order is fixed.
Multilinearity reduces the calculation to basis insertions, with their antisymmetric signs.
steps: Choose a canonical symplectic basis for the odd form.

An invertible antisymmetric form has paired basis directions. In these coordinates the fermionic Gaussian is a product over independent two-variable blocks, and its integral is the nonzero Pfaffian of $-B$.
Check the ordered basis insertions block by block.

By multilinearity, it suffices to take each linear insertion to be a coordinate function. A block contributes only if both of its variables are selected, or neither is selected and the quadratic exponential supplies them. An odd total insertion count therefore gives zero.
Sum the signed pairings in basis-independent form.

Moving selected odd variables into their volume order contributes the permutation sign of the matching. The remaining factors are the inverse-form entries. Their signed sum is precisely the Pfaffian of the contraction matrix. Divide by the common Gaussian Pfaffian to obtain the normalized formula.
app: Evaluate a four-fermion correlation with fixed order
The insertions are ordered as 1,2,3,4 and the Gaussian covariance is antisymmetric.
The four-point Pfaffian is $C_{12}C_{34}-C_{13}C_{24}+C_{14}C_{23}$.
Substitution gives $1\times2-3\times4+5\times6=20$.
The ordered four-fermion Gaussian expectation is 20.

drafts.name: Finite CAR algebra has a unique irreducible Fock representation
drafts.statement: For n complex fermionic modes, the canonical anticommutation relations $\{a_i,a_j^{\dagger}\}=\delta_{ij}$ and $\{a_i,a_j\}=0$ define the matrix algebra $M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$. Its irreducible [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) representation on the fermionic [Hilbert space](c:hilbert-space) is unique up to unitary equivalence and has dimension $2^n$.
hyps: There are finitely many complex modes with the standard CAR and the adjoint relation.
The finite CAR permits ordered normal monomials and a positive Fock representation.
Representations are nonzero irreducible star representations over the complex numbers.
The full finite matrix algebra has only its defining irreducible star representation.
steps: Represent the modes by exterior multiplication and contraction.
On $\Lambda(\mathbb C^n)$, let $a_i^{\dagger}$ multiply by the i-th basis vector and let $a_i$ contract with it. These operations obey the CAR, and the occupation basis has $2^n$ vectors.
Construct all matrix units from the CAR operators.

The vacuum projector is $P_0=\prod_i(1-a_i^{\dagger}a_i)$. Products $a_I^{\dagger}P_0a_J$, with their ordering signs fixed, send one occupation vector to another and annihilate the others. They span all matrix units on the Fock space.
Compare the dimension bound and classify irreducible representations.

The CAR rewrites any word as a linear combination of at most $4^n$ ordered monomials. The represented algebra already has dimension $(2^n)^2=4^n$, so the representation is an isomorphism onto the full matrix algebra. Every irreducible star representation of this algebra is unitarily equivalent to its defining one.
app: Count the Fock states of three fermionic modes
Take $n=3$ independent complex modes.
Use the standard finite CAR and an irreducible nonzero star representation.
The occupation numbers are each 0 or 1, so there are $2^3=8$ basis states.
The CAR algebra is therefore $M_8(\mathbb C)$, with vector-space dimension $8^2=64$.
The unique irreducible Fock representation has 8 states.

drafts.name: Free fermion path integral with periodic time equals a normalized supertrace
drafts.statement: For a fully massive even-dimensional free fermionic [quantum field theory](c:quantum-field-theory) on a time circle of length L, its ordered periodic [path integral](c:path-integral) correlator equals $\operatorname{sTr}(\psi(t_1)\cdots\psi(t_n)e^{-LH})/\operatorname{sTr}(e^{-LH})$, with the source Wick-rotation convention. Periodic fermions give a supertrace, rather than the ordinary thermal trace.
hyps: The free fermion Hamiltonian has finitely many nonzero masses, with an even-dimensional one-particle real space.
The Fock Hamiltonian factorizes into independent modes and the supertrace denominator is nonzero.
The Euclidean time circle has periodic fermionic boundary conditions and the insertions are time ordered.
Periodic sewing inserts the grading operator into the trace, with the corresponding fermionic signs.
steps: Diagonalize the free Hamiltonian into independent fermion modes.
The source constructs the Clifford Fock space and writes $H=\sum_jm_j(2N_j-1)$ with $m_j>0$. Each occupation number $N_j$ is 0 or 1, and parity is $(-1)^{\sum_jN_j}$.
Sew the periodic Grassmann path integral with the parity insertion.

The finite-mode coherent-state calculation identifies a periodic Grassmann time boundary with a trace containing $(-1)^F$. Time-ordered insertions remain inside this trace. Antiperiodic sewing would instead give the ordinary trace.
Compare contractions and divide by the partition function.

The source free propagator is the inverse of the periodic first-order kinetic operator. The Fock supertrace has the same two-point contraction, and the fermionic Wick theorem fixes every higher product. The denominator factorizes as $\prod_j(e^{Lm_j}-e^{-Lm_j})$, which is nonzero for positive L and nonzero masses.
app: Compute a one-mode periodic fermion partition function
Take one complex mode with $m=1$ and circle length $L=1$.
The mass is nonzero and the boundary condition is periodic.
The empty mode has energy -1 and even parity. The occupied mode has energy +1 and odd parity.
The supertrace is therefore $e^1-e^{-1}=2\sinh1$. The ordinary antiperiodic thermal partition function would be $e^1+e^{-1}$.
The periodic fermion partition function is $2\sinh1$.
